Polonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Po and atomic number 84.
Spironolactone: Pfizer. Spironolactone, sold under the brand name Aldactone among others, is classed as a diuretic medication.
In which country did the Chengdu J-10 take place?

Chengdu J-10: People's Republic of China. It is produced by the Chengdu Aircraft Corporation (CAC) for the People's Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) of China, and exported to the Pakistan Air Force (PAF).
Who is credited with discovering Seaborgium?
Seaborgium: Yuri Oganessian. Seaborgium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Sg and atomic number 106.
Who is credited with discovering Hydrogen cyanide?
Hydrogen cyanide: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Hydrogen cyanide (also called prussic acid) is a chemical compound with the formula HCN and structural formula H−C≡N.
Who is credited with discovering Tungsten?
Tungsten: Juan José Elhuyar. Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
This genus of succulent, spiky-leaved plants native to the arid Americas typically takes years to mature, with each rosette flowering only once before dying — what's the genus called?
Agave (Anglo-Hispanic) is a genus of monocots native to the arid regions of the Americas.
In 1978, a run-in with a particle accelerator's proton beam left this Russian physicist with an extraordinary survival story after it passed straight through his head — who is he?
Anatoli Bugorski (born 25 June 1942) is a Russian retired particle physicist.
This red giant is the brightest star in the constellation Boötes and the fourth-brightest star in the entire night sky — name the star?
Arcturus is a red giant star in the northern constellation of Botes, and the brightest star in the constellation.
The only mammals capable of true sustained flight, members of this order — the second largest among mammals — fly using long digits webbed by a thin membrane. What are they?
Bat (order Chiroptera) are winged mammals, the only mammals capable of true and sustained flight.
Native to cool parts of Europe and Asia, this deciduous shrub produces small, glossy black berries especially rich in vitamin C and vulnerable to cold snaps during spring flowering — name the fruit?
Blackcurrant (Ribes nigrum), black currant or cassis is a deciduous shrub in the family Grossulariaceae grown for its edible berries.
Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide and often striking during sleep, this parafunctional habit grinds teeth and clenches jaws until enamel wears away — what's it called?
Bruxism is excessive teeth grinding or jaw clenching.

Which German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist discovered oxygen — though Priestley published first — and identified elements like molybdenum, tungsten, and chlorine before reportedly dying of mercury poisoning?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele (9 December 1742 - 21 May 1786) was a German-Swedish pharmaceutical chemist.

Sold under the brand name Thorazine, this phenothiazine antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder — but it's also been used for nausea, pre-surgery anxiety, and even stubborn hiccups. What is it?
Chlorpromazine (CPZ), marketed under the brand names Thorazine and Largactil among others, is an antipsychotic medication.
Native to Asia but so invasive in Australian cities that it was dubbed 'Most Important Pest/Problem' in 2008, which urban-adapted bird species is this?
Common myna (Acridotheres tristis), sometimes spelled mynah, is a bird in the family Sturnidae, native to Asia.
This bluish-purple discoloration of the skin, most visible on the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes, signals a drop in oxygen bound to hemoglobin in the blood — name the condition?
Cyanosis is the change of tissue color to a bluish-purple hue, as a result of decrease in the amount of oxygen bound to the hemoglobin in the red blood cells of the capillary bed.
Bred around 1890 in Thuringia by a tax collector seeking a loyal protector, this German working-dog breed is known in North America by a slightly different two-word name — which breed?
Dobermann is a German breed of medium-large working dog of pinscher type.

This German chess champion — also a mathematician and philosopher — held the world title for 27 years, the longest reign ever, and was famed for a 'psychological' approach said to unsettle opponents. Who was he?
Emanuel Lasker (German; December 24, 1868 - January 11, 1941) was a German chess player, mathematician, and philosopher.

This front-of-the-head feature found in humans and other animals houses most of the sense organs, including the eyes, nose, and mouth, and its damage can profoundly affect one's sense of identity — name this body part?
Face is the front of the head in humans and many other animals that features most of the sense organs including the eyes, nose and mouth.
Having led Renault, Sauber, and Alfa Romeo's F1 outfits, this French engineer took the reins at Ferrari as team principal in 2023 — who is he?
Fred Vasseur (French; born 28 May 1968) is a French motorsport executive, businessman and engineer.

Colorless, odorless, and oddly sweet, this viscous sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of every triglyceride in animal fat, and moonlights as a food sweetener — what is it?
Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Hailed by Time as a 2019 'Pioneer' yet condemned as a mad scientist, which Chinese biophysicist announced in 2018 that he'd created the first gene-edited human babies?
He Jiankui (pinyin: H Jinku HUH KWAY; born 1984) is a Chinese biophysicist known for his controversial first use of genome editing in humans in 2018.
While first described from Virginia, this genus of flowering shrubs reaches its greatest diversity in East Asia, and some species climb up to 30 metres by scaling trees. What plant is it?
Hydrangea (or) is a genus of more than 70 species of flowering plants native to Asia and the Americas.
These creatures don't breathe through a nose or lungs — air enters through tiny paired openings along their sides, piped straight to the tissues. What hexapod group are they?
Insect (from Latin insectum) are hexapod invertebrates of the class Insecta.
This financier's 1999 bestseller on mutual funds became an investment classic after he founded a low-cost investing giant — who is he?

John C. Bogle (May 8, 1929 - January 16, 2019) was an American investor, business magnate and philanthropist who was the founder of The Vanguard Group and is credited with popularizing the index fund.
Alongside Robert Goddard and Hermann Oberth, this reclusive Russian scientist who lived in a log house near Kaluga is considered a founding father of modern rocketry — who is he?

This scientific discipline studies language through areas like syntax, semantics, morphology, and phonology, with subfields examining its biological roots and psychological underpinnings — name the field?
Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguistics encompasses many branches and subfields that span both theoretical and practical applications.

With degrees from Stanford in chemical engineering and a medical degree from Cornell, this physician-astronaut spent nearly eight days aboard Endeavour in 1992, becoming the first African-American woman in space — who is she?
Mae Jemison (born October 17, 1956) is an American engineer, physician, and former NASA astronaut.
Most common on the legs in women and the back in men, this cancer develops from melanin-producing skin cells and, in extremely rare cases, can even arise in the lungs — which cancer?
Melanoma is a type of cancer, typically skin cancer; it develops from the melanin-producing cells known as melanocytes.
These cylindrical, burrowing insects have small eyes and shovel-like front limbs highly adapted for digging underground — name the family?
Mole cricket are members of the insect family Gryllotalpidae, in the order Orthoptera (grasshoppers, locusts, and crickets).
This flexible body part lets the head turn in every direction while its compartments guard the spinal cord and upper airway between head and torso — what is it, also known as the cervix?
Neck is the part of the body in many vertebrates that connects the head to the torso.
Named after a German physicist, this SI unit of electrical resistance is represented by the uppercase Greek letter omega — name the unit?
Ohm (symbol:, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).

This skin sensation — often described as tingling, prickling, or numbness — is most familiar as the 'pins and needles' feeling after a limb falls asleep from staying still too long — name this sensation?
Paresthesia (or paraesthesia) is a sensation of the skin that may feel like numbness (hypoesthesia), tingling, pricking, chilling, or burning.
Colorless in acid and a vivid pink in base, which phthalein dye is the chemist's go-to indicator for acid-base titrations?
Phenolphthalein (feh-NOL(F)-th-leen) is a chemical compound with the formula C20H14O4 and is often written as "HIn", "HPh", "phph" or simply "Ph" in shorthand notation.

This academic field studies systems of governance and power, favoring descriptive and empirical analysis of behavior and institutions over the value judgments used in philosophy about the state — name the discipline?
Political science (sometimes abbreviated as poli sci) is a field which aims to study the scientific aspect of politics.

This medical specialty diagnoses, treats, and prevents disorders of cognition, perception, mood, emotion, and behavior, typically beginning assessment with a case history and mental status exam — name the field?
Psychiatry is the medical specialty devoted to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of deleterious mental conditions.
One of the three ancient arts of discourse alongside grammar and logic, this discipline studies the techniques speakers and writers use to inform, persuade, and motivate an audience — what is it?
Rhetoric is the art of persuasion.
Which plant genus in the mint family, comprising nearly 1,000 species of shrubs and perennials, includes both a common cooking herb and — surprisingly — rosemary as one of its species?
Salvia is the largest genus of plants in the sage family Lamiaceae, with just under 1,000 species of shrubs, herbaceous perennials, and annuals.

Though many are crustaceans more closely related to insects than to fish, which group of exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates, including molluscs and echinoderms, is a leading cause of food allergies?
Shellfish are exoskeleton-bearing aquatic invertebrates used as food, including various species of molluscs, crustaceans, and echinoderms.

Extending from the base of the brainstem down to the lower back, this tubular bundle of nervous tissue is covered by the meninges and, together with the brain, makes up the central nervous system — name this structure?

Spinal cord is a long, thin, tubular structure made up of nervous tissue that extends from the medulla oblongata in the lower brainstem to the lumbar region of the vertebral column (backbone) of vertebrate animals.
Also called 'true comfrey,' this Boraginaceae perennial is native to damp European meadows and popular with bumblebees, despite carrying warnings about liver toxicity if eaten — which plant?
Symphytum officinale is a perennial flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae.
This condition causes abnormally low platelet levels in the blood, leading to prolonged or excessive bleeding — what blood disorder is it?
Thrombocytopenia is a condition characterized by abnormally low levels of platelets (also known as thrombocytes) in the blood.
The most widespread New World scavenger of its kind, this bird sniffs out the gases of early decay to find carrion and rides thermals instead of flapping — which bird?
Turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) is the most widespread of the New World vultures.

Its small molecule packs a surprising punch: strong polarity, relentless hydrogen bonding, and a starring role as the fluid of all known life and the main stuff of Earth's oceans — what compound is it?
Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O.

Released from prison in June 2025 to resume leading Turkey's nationalist Victory Party, this politician previously served as deputy leader of the far-right Nationalist Movement Party in the mid-2010s — who is he?
Ümit Özdağ (born 3 March 1961) is a Turkish politician who returned to his position as the current leader of the Victory Party after being released from prison on 17 June 2025.
Recognizable by its black-and-white striped legs and a lyre-shaped marking on its thorax, this mosquito native to North Africa spreads dengue and yellow fever worldwide — what is it?
Aedes aegypti: Species of mosquito. The mosquito can be recognized by black and white markings on its legs and a marking in the form of a lyre on the upper surface of its thorax.
This diverse group of photosynthetic organisms ranges from microscopic plankton to seaweeds 50 metres long — yet excludes the land plants entirely. What is it?
Algae: Diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. Algae (AL-jee, UK also AL-ghee; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.
Nominated by Donald Trump in 2020, this Notre Dame law professor became the fifth woman to serve as a US Supreme Court associate justice after previously sitting on the Seventh Circuit — who is she?

Amy Coney Barrett: US Supreme Court justice since 2020. Barrett graduated from Rhodes College before attending Notre Dame Law School, earning a Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree in 1997 and ranked first in her class.
Unlike fear, which responds to a threat that's already here, this emotional state involves dread over something that hasn't happened yet, often paired with pacing and rumination. What is it?
About 200 times sweeter than table sugar, this artificial sweetener sold as NutraSweet and Equal had its FDA approval briefly revoked before being re-approved in 1981 — what is it?

Native to West and Central Africa, this nonvenomous constrictor is the smallest of its kind on the continent and earns its common name from its habit of curling into a tight coil when frightened — which species?
Ball python: Species of constricting snake.
Both heads of this upper-arm muscle originate on the scapula and let you flex your elbow while turning your palm upward — what muscle is it?

Biceps: Muscle on the front of the upper arm. While the long head of the biceps crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, its main function is at the elbow where it flexes and supinates the forearm.

Flying for the U.S. Air Force since 1955, this subsonic strategic bomber evolved from a six-turboprop straight-wing design into eight swept-wing turbojets and can haul up to 70,000 pounds of weapons — what's its name?
Boeing B-52 Stratofortress: American strategic bomber aircraft.

This Italian-American physicist invented an improved coincidence circuit and traveled to Eritrea to prove cosmic rays arrive more strongly from the West than the East, before Italy's racial laws forced him to flee — who was he?
Which multidrug-resistant fungal yeast colonizes skin in long-term care facilities and causes bloodstream infections with up to a 60% mortality rate?
Named after a Louisiana parish and named the state's official canine in 1979, this herding breed was traditionally used to hunt feral boars — what breed is it?
Catahoula Leopard Dog: American breed of dog.
Sometimes dubbed the 'central science' for sitting between physics and biology, this field studies how matter is composed, behaves, and transforms in reactions — what is it?
Chemistry: Scientific study of matter's behavior and properties.
Named after the French missionary who propagated it in Algeria, this citrus hybrid of mandarin and sweet orange is often sold as an 'Easy-peeler' — which fruit?
Clementine: Hybrid citrus fruit. The exterior is a deep orange colour with a smooth, glossy appearance.
Best known for its powerful, beautiful song, this small Old World flycatcher sometimes hybridizes with a closely related thrush species where their ranges overlap — which bird?
Common nightingale: Species of bird. Its range partly overlaps with that of the more northerly thrush nightingale (Luscinia luscinia), a closely related species with which hybrids have occurred.
Broken down from creatine phosphate in muscle metabolism, this compound is released into the blood at a rate tied to a person's muscle mass — what is it?
Creatinine: Breakdown product of creatine phosphate.
Also called thornapple or devil's trumpet, this genus of nine highly poisonous nightshade plants lent its American name to an outbreak in colonial Jamestown — what genus is it?
Datura: Genus of poisonous, potentially psychoactive plants.

This colourless, water-mixable lab solvent is technically odorless — but degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity. It's better known by a three-letter abbreviation; what's the compound?
Dimethylformamide: Chemical compound. Dimethylformamide, DMF is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.
This German-born British economist championed 'human-scale, appropriate technology' in his 1973 book, later ranked among the 100 most influential books since World War II — who was he?
E. F. Schumacher: British statistician and economist (1911–1977)
This messenger network of hormone feedback loops releases chemicals from internal glands like the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal glands straight into the bloodstream to regulate distant organs?
Endocrine system: Hormone-producing glands of a body.

A women's-rights campaigner schooled in 1830s New York, she was the first scientist to show certain gases trap heat — anticipating that rising CO2 could warm the climate. Who was this overlooked pioneer?
Eunice Newton Foote: American scientist and activist (1819–1888)
This genus of small-to-medium wildcats — ranging from the diminutive black-footed cat to the larger jungle cat — also includes humanity's domestic pet, the housecat — which genus?
Home to the radius and ulna joined by the interosseous membrane, this region of the arm lies between the elbow and the wrist — what is it?
Forearm: Region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist.
Often triggered by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, this inflammation of the stomach lining can, in its autoimmune form, lead to pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis: Inflammation of the stomach lining. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.
Produced by the pancreas's alpha cells, this hormone raises blood sugar by triggering the liver to break down stored glycogen — the functional opposite of insulin. What is it?
Glucagon: Peptide hormone. It raises the concentration of glucose and fatty acids in the bloodstream and is considered to be the main catabolic hormone of the body.
Closely related to the llama, this wild South American camelid shares its range with a higher-altitude cousin, the vicuña — what is it?

First proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos, this astronomical model places the sun rather than the Earth at the center of the universe. What is this superseded model called?
Heliocentrism: Sun-centered astronomical model. Historically, heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed Earth at the center.
Nicknamed 'handy man' for its toolmaking, this archaic human species lived in East and South Africa as far back as 2.4 million years ago — which species?
Homo habilis: Archaic human species from 2.4 to 1.65 mya.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.
The abbreviation SI, used for the modern metric system, comes from its official name in which language?
Systeme international d'unites. The Bureau International des Poids et Mesures that maintains it sits outside Paris, which is why the naming is French rather than English.
A French soldier turned naturalist, this early proponent of biological evolution published the three-volume 'Flore françoise' and joined the French Academy of Sciences in 1779 — who is he?
Nicknamed 'Iron Annie,' which corrugated-skin transport plane began life as a 1930 civilian airliner before Nazi Germany converted it for military use?
These paired skin folds run from the mons pubis to the perineum and are considered the anatomical counterpart to the male scrotum — what are they called?
Labia majora: Folds of skin that contain and protect the vulva's other parts.
Also sold as Xylocaine, this amino-amide local anesthetic numbs in minutes and doubles as a treatment for dangerous ventricular heart rhythms — what is it?
Lidocaine: Local anesthetic. Lidocaine, also known as lignocaine and sold under the brand name Xylocaine among others, is a local anesthetic of the amino amide type.

Credited as a 'Father of Cinematography,' this French artist filmed the Roundhay Garden Scene in Leeds in 1888 — then vanished without a trace two years later, and his work never shaped commercial cinema. Who was he?
Louis Le Prince: French motion-picture pioneer (1841–1890s)
Defined by milk-producing glands, hair or fur, a broad neocortex, and three tiny middle-ear bones, this animal class split from reptile-and-bird ancestors over 300 million years ago — what is it?
Mammal: Class of animals with milk-producing glands.
The larval stage of a darkling beetle, this insect is used in biomedical research, eaten as a food source for animals and humans, and is also a common food-storage pest — what is it called?
Mealworm: Species of darkling beetle, larval form.
This development economist shared the 2019 Nobel with Esther Duflo and Abhijit Banerjee for an experimental approach to fighting global poverty — who is he?
Michael Kremer: American economist and Nobel laureate (born 1964)
Originally a dry-season staple for ǃKung hunter-gatherers, this tropical vine in the Cucurbitaceae family produces an intensely bitter edible fruit widely used across Asian cuisine — what is it?
Momordica charantia: Species of plant in the gourd family.

It strikes when blood flow to the heart muscle stops, killing tissue — classically a crushing chest pain that radiates to the left arm or jaw, though women more often feel only neck pain or fatigue. What is this medical emergency?
Myocardial infarction: Interruption of cardiac blood supply.
This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not Earth, at the center of the universe in a book published just before his death in 1543 — kicking off a revolution in science. Who was he?

With atomic number 118, this synthetic element boasts the highest atomic number and mass of any known element, and was named to honor the physicist who led the hunt for the periodic table's heaviest members — what is it?
Oganesson: Chemical element with atomic number 118 (Og)
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compound pairs oxygen with another element — the same chemistry behind the thin protective layer on aluminium foil — what is it called?
Oxide: Compounds containing an oxygen atom.
The males of this pheasant-family bird are famed for piercing calls and extravagant plumage; its Asiatic, green, and Congo species span India to central Africa — what common name covers them all?
Peafowl: Group of large game birds.
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive fear that persists more than six months and can trigger fainting in blood-or-injury cases — what is it?
Phobia: Anxiety disorder classified by a persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Downgraded from planet to dwarf in 2006 when astronomers adopted a new definition, this Kuiper belt object orbits beyond Neptune—what celestial body is it?
Pluto: Largest dwarf planet. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).
Once one of America's leading rocket experts with an MIT aeronautics degree, he was deported to China in 1955 and went on to father that nation's space program — which aerospace engineer?

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
A luminous ball of plasma held together by its own gravity, the closest example to Earth is the Sun — what celestial object is this?
Star: Large self-illuminated object in space.
Striking suddenly and resolving — one way or another — within 8 to 10 hours, this mysterious epidemic first hit England in 1485 and vanished after a final outbreak in 1551 — what was it called?
Sweating sickness: Contagious disease in Europe, 1485–1551.
Made of collagen like its bone-to-bone cousin the ligament, this tough band of connective tissue instead links muscle to bone, and there are about 4,000 of them in your body — what is it called?
Tendon: Type of tissue that connects muscle to bone.
Native to Africa and the Middle East, this freshwater fish has become a global aquaculture staple but can turn invasive in warm habitats like Australia — which fish?
Tilapia: Common name for many species of fish.
This essential amino acid, which the body can't make on its own, is a precursor to serotonin, melatonin, and vitamin B3 — which amino acid?
Found in Central and South America, only three living species of this blood-feeding, leaf-nosed flying mammal exist, while two extinct relatives once roamed North America — which creature?

The smallest member of this genus, found in Great Britain, is also considered the tiniest carnivorous mammal species on Earth, with some populations turning white in winter. What group of small predators is this?
Weasel: Mammal of the mustelid family.
Known to TV audiences as 'Dr. Now,' this Iranian-born American surgeon has spent over a decade helping patients on My 600-lb Life reach life-saving weight loss — who is he?
Younan Nowzaradan: Iranian-American surgeon, television personality, and author (born 1944)

The symbol for arsenic is As. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
What is the chemical symbol for nihonium?
The symbol for nihonium is Nh. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.
